method: US and European fabs, packaging and materials sites (including one project cancelled in Nov 2026), the EU IPCEI ME/CT and the Dutch Project Beethoven, and equipment models (Lam, Applied Materials, Teradyne, Advantest, ASM, NAURA, TEL), from company releases, government pages, product pages and industry news located by web search; titles and search-result summaries.

pr.tech: Conductor etch with DirectDrive solid-state plasma source (responds about 100x faster than earlier sources, per Lam), TEMPO plasma pulsing and SNAP ion-energy control; successor to the Kiyo line
pr.app: Gate-all-around transistors, 6F2 DRAM and 3D NAND; extendable to 4F2 DRAM, CFET and 3D DRAM (per Lam)
pr.note: Batch 16: launched 19 Feb 2025; details from Lam's release as republished; performance figures are the company's claims.

pr.tech: Molybdenum atomic layer deposition; no adhesion or barrier layer needed (unlike tungsten); more than 50 % lower resistance than conventional tungsten in most instances (per Lam)
pr.app: Interconnect and wordline metallisation (in volume production at Micron for NAND, per Lam)
pr.note: Batch 16: launched 19 Feb 2025 alongside Akara; resistance figure is a company claim.

pr.tech: eBeam metrology with cold field emission (CFE): up to 50 % higher resolution and up to 10x faster imaging than thermal field emission (per Applied); sub-nanometre multi-layer imaging
pr.app: EUV overlay, nanosheet measurement and epi void detection in GAA logic, backside power delivery, DRAM and 3D NAND
pr.note: Batch 16: introduced 7 Oct 2025 alongside Kinex and Xtera; performance figures are company claims.

pr.tech: HBM memory tester: HBM2E to HBM4E, data rates up to 4.5 Gbps, up to 9,216 digital pins and 2,560 power pins; Logic Vector Memory option for logic base dies (per Teradyne)
pr.app: HBM base-die wafer test, pre- and post-singulation stack test, memory core and speed test
pr.note: Batch 16: launched 4 Aug 2025; volume shipments ramping at the largest HBM makers (per Teradyne). Throughput claim (1.6x) is the company's.

pr.tech: DRAM and NAND tester for wafer sort and final test: up to 2,048 devices in parallel at wafer and 512 at package; up to 2.4 Gbps (per Advantest)
pr.app: DRAM and NAND flash wafer and package test
pr.note: Batch 16: launched 17 Jul 2015 (per Electronic Design); HBM support is not claimed for this model.

pr.tech: High-speed memory tester with 16,256 channels (per Advantest)
pr.app: SDRAM, DDR4, LPDDR4 and high-bandwidth memory (HBM) test
pr.note: Batch 16: from the Advantest product page summary.

pr.tech: Single-wafer ALD reactor; up to four modules on the XP cluster platform; AXIS reactor package for uniformity and repeatability (per ASM)
pr.app: High-k gate dielectrics (hafnium oxide, hafnium silicate)
pr.note: Batch 16: from the ASM product page summary.

pr.tech: Showerhead-based ALD process module for thin conformal metal and dielectric layers (per ASM)
pr.app: Metal gate stacks and capacitor electrodes
pr.note: Batch 16: from the ASM product page summary.

pr.tech: 12-inch die-to-wafer (D2W) hybrid bonder; among the first in China to complete customer-side D2W process verification (per report)
pr.note: Batch 16: launched March 2026 at SEMICON China (per coverage).

pr.tech: Gas cluster beam system that modifies the critical dimension and shape of EUV-formed patterns, with wafer-scanning control of the etch amount at any point (per TEL)
pr.app: EUV pattern refinement: fewer multi-patterning steps, lower line-edge roughness
pr.note: Batch 16: announced August 2024 (per TEL release summary).

fa.name: Intel Fab 52, Ocotillo campus (Chandler, Arizona)
fa.capacity: Not disclosed (Intel has not published capacity; ramp continues into 2026, per coverage)
fa.products: Panther Lake and Clearwater Forest processors, among other Intel 18A products (per Intel press kit)
fa.notes: Intel's fifth high-volume fab at Ocotillo; under construction since 2021. Mass production reported from July 2025 and the formal opening on 9 Oct 2025 (per heise).

fa.name: Intel Fab 34, Leixlip (Ireland)

invest.label: €17 billion (per The Irish Times; Intel's page summary showed '17 million', which looks like an error)

fa.capacity: Doubled Intel's manufacturing capacity in Ireland (per The Irish Times)
fa.notes: High-volume production of Intel 4 began 29 Sept 2023: Intel's first EUV high-volume manufacturing in Europe.

fa.name: STMicroelectronics silicon carbide campus, Catania
fa.scheme: Italian state aid of about €2 billion approved by the European Commission, with EU Chips Act backing (per coverage)
fa.technology: Integrated silicon carbide, from substrate to module
fa.notes: ST said production would begin in 2026, with full capacity by 2033 (plans, per Bloomberg). An earlier, separate €292.5 million grant (Oct 2022) supported a SiC substrate plant in Catania. Construction progress not found in reviewed sources.

fa.name: Silicon Box chiplet integration facility, Novara
fa.scheme: Italian state aid of €1.3 billion approved by the European Commission (Dec 2024); Open EU Foundry status under the European Chips Act (Mar 2026), per coverage
fa.notes: Original plan: construction from 2H 2025 and initial production in 1Q 2028, with full capacity in 2033. Groundbreaking not confirmed in reviewed sources; the March 2026 Open EU Foundry status was reported to speed up construction approvals.

fa.name: Micron New York megafab, Clay

invest.label: Up to US$100 billion for up to four fabs (per coverage)

fa.jobs: About 50,000 in New York (direct and indirect, per Micron)
fa.notes: Groundbreaking 16 Jan 2026 after environmental delays; foundation work began about six months later. The first two fabs are planned to come online in 2030 and the rest by 2041 (plans). Bechtel is the EPC contractor for phase one (per coverage).

fa.name: GlobalWafers 300 mm silicon wafer plant, Sherman
fa.scheme: US CHIPS and Science Act direct funding: up to $406 million across Texas and Missouri, $380 million for Sherman (per NIST)

invest.label: About US$3.5 billion plant (per Evertiq); an additional US$4 billion was announced at opening

fa.capacity: Earlier plans targeted 1.2 million 300 mm wafers per month at full build-out (per Tom's Hardware)
fa.technology: Fully integrated 300 mm silicon wafer production
fa.notes: Grand opening 15 May 2025: the first of three planned Sherman fabs. Investment figures differ across announcements (US$5 billion in 2022, US$3.5 billion for the opened plant, and US$4 billion of expansion) and are not reconciled.

fa.name: Texas Instruments LFAB2, Lehi (Utah)

invest.label: US$11 billion, the largest economic investment in Utah's history (per TI)

fa.notes: Will connect to LFAB1, which started production in Dec 2022. TI's page still describes LFAB2 as under construction, with production as early as 2026 (a plan). Designed for LEED Gold, with a goal of 100 % renewable electricity.

fa.name: Wolfspeed Mohawk Valley silicon carbide fab, Marcy (New York)

invest.label: About US$1 billion (per NY Governor's Office)

fa.technology: 200 mm silicon carbide device fab; fully automated, automotive-qualified (per Wolfspeed)
fa.jobs: Over 600 within the first eight years (per NY Governor's Office)
fa.notes: Opened 25 Apr 2022; the first SiC lot ran earlier that month. Substrates are to come from the John Palmour centre (FAC-000043). A later plan to raise capacity by about 30 % is not recorded as a milestone.

fa.name: GlobalFoundries Dresden expansion (Project SPRINT)
fa.scheme: German federal and Free State of Saxony funding under European Chips Act rules (expected, per coverage)
fa.capacity: More than one million wafers a year by end-2028 (plan); current baseline figures differ between sources
fa.technology: Automotive, aerospace, industrial IoT and defence processes; FDX platforms
fa.notes: Work began in June 2025 at GF's own risk, before the EU state-aid review concluded (per Silicon Saxony); the project was announced on 28 Oct 2025. A topping-out milestone was reported later (date not captured).

fa.name: onsemi silicon carbide expansion, Rožnov pod Radhoštěm (cancelled)
fa.scheme: Czech state aid of €450 million approved by the European Commission (per coverage); status of the aid after cancellation unclear

invest.label: Up to US$2 billion planned (brownfield, multi-year)

fa.notes: onsemi and the Czech Ministry of Industry and Trade agreed not to proceed (Nov 2026), citing the global semiconductor and SiC markets. Existing production at Rožnov and Brno continues. Kept as a record: cancelled projects are history, not deleted.

pg.name: IPCEI on Microelectronics and Communication Technologies (IPCEI ME/CT)

facts.label: Approved
facts.value: 8 June 2023 by the European Commission under EU state-aid rules

facts.label: Public support
facts.value: Up to €8.1 billion from 14 Member States, expected to unlock €13.7 billion of private investment

facts.label: Scope
facts.value: R&D and first industrial deployment across the microelectronics and communication value chain, from materials and tools to chip design and manufacturing

pg.name: Netherlands Project Beethoven (Brainport Eindhoven chip ecosystem package)

facts.label: Announced
facts.value: 28 March 2024: about €2.51 billion from central government and regional authorities for education, knowledge and spatial infrastructure

facts.label: Funding split (differs)
facts.value: Government.nl cites €1.28 billion from the National Growth Fund; Holland High Tech cites a €1.73 billion government contribution
